reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) demonstrates M–N bond formation and durability benefits in an N–Pt/HEA electrocatalyst for ORR, but it does not address automotive exhaust conditions (CO/hydrocarbon oxidation, H2O/NO poisoning, low-temperature activity below 150 °C) or the specific Cu–Ni-based alloy composition proposed. The key premise that these M–N bond benefits will transfer to the entirely different catalytic application and material system is unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Nitrogen doping of a multi-principal-element alloy via NH3 annealing creates stable M–N bonds that enhance catalytic activity and durability.
M–N bonds in a high-entropy alloy matrix can stabilize active metal atoms and reduce sintering.
The beneficial effects of M–N bonds observed in electrocatalysis (ORR) will translate to automotive exhaust oxidation under low-temperature, poisoning, and aging conditions.
The proposed NH3 annealing treatment is applicable to a near-equiatomic alloy containing Cu, Ni, and small amounts of platinum-group metals to form the desired M–N bonds.
